segments.translation: 因为他感觉自己与宇宙合一，从字面上看，他决定创建这个研究所，不仅研究他一直在研究的外层空间，而且还研究内部空间，以探索内部空间。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So I remember in college reading about this new institute and their motto was the exploring the frontiers of consciousness.
segments.translation: 所以我记得在大学里读到过关于这个新研究所的文章，他们的座右铭是探索意识的前沿。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And they thought, that sounds like something I want to do, but there wasn't any place to do that other than this one institute.
segments.translation: 他们认为，这听起来像是我想做的事情，但除了这个研究所之外，没有任何地方可以做这件事。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So I always had in the back of my mind that that's that's where I want to end up.
segments.translation: 所以我一直在心里认为这就是我想要的结局。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: What is that term noetic?
segments.translation: 意念这个词是什么？

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I know I've heard it before but I I never looked it up.
segments.translation: 我知道我以前听说过，但我从未查过。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Noetic.
segments.translation: 意念。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So noetic is a feeling of intuition, except that it carries a sense of certainty that the intuition is correct.
segments.translation: 因此，意念是一种直觉的感觉，只不过它带有一种直觉是正确的确定感。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So intuition is knowing something without knowing how you know.
segments.translation: 所以直觉就是知道某事而不知道你是如何知道的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It just sort of arrives, but it's knowing with with certainty and more often than not the certainty is correct.
segments.translation: 它只是到达了，但它是确定性地知道的，而且这种确定性往往是正确的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So people talk about downloads and meditation and other places.
segments.translation: 所以人们谈论下载和冥想等地方。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: That's what that is.
segments.translation: 就是这样。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: This is a subject that up until, I would say last couple decades was pretty openly dismissed by rational people, right?
segments.translation: 我想说，直到过去几十年，这个话题一直被理性的人公开驳回，对吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: There's, there's almost like a desire to dismiss it, like a desire to define the world in much clearer terms where you, it's maybe ego driven, you're in control of your own destiny.
segments.translation: 几乎就像是一种想要驳回它的愿望，就像一种想要以更清晰的方式定义世界的愿望，在这个世界中，你可能是自我驱动的，你掌控着自己的命运。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And then there's certain factors that are out of your control and just this is how it is and this is life, deal with it.
segments.translation: 然后有些因素是你无法控制的，事情就是这样，这就是生活，应对它。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And all this mystical woo woo magic bullshit that people have been talking about for some strange reason for thousands of years, we just dismiss and we dismiss it under the narrative of science.
segments.translation: 几千年来，人们出于某种奇怪的原因一直在谈论所有这些神秘的、神奇的废话，我们只是不予理睬，我们在科学的叙述下不理睬它。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: We're talking about science.
segments.translation: 我们正在谈论科学。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: We're science people.
segments.translation: 我们是科学人。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: We want data, but there is data.
segments.translation: 我们想要数据，但数据已经存在。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: That's what's weird.
segments.translation: 这就是奇怪的地方。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And if you're willing to look a little preposterous, which I certainly am, I think it's a good thing to do every now and then.
segments.translation: 如果你愿意表现得有点荒谬（我确实是这样），我认为时不时地这样做是一件好事。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Take a fucking chance and try to figure out if the world is exactly constructed the way you've been told.
segments.translation: 抓住一个他妈的机会，试着弄清楚这个世界是否完全按照你所说的方式构建。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Because it might not be.
segments.translation: 因为可能不是。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: There might be some weirdness to it all.
segments.translation: 这一切可能有些奇怪。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And it seems like we all agree.
segments.translation: 看来我们都同意。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: We all agree there is some weirdness.
segments.translation: 我们都同意有一些奇怪的地方。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: You could chalk it off to coincidence.
segments.translation: 你可以把它归结为巧合。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: When you think about a person and you haven't thought about them forever and all sudden they call you, there's there's some weirdness in the world.
segments.translation: 当你想起一个人，而你并没有永远想起他们，突然他们打电话给你时，世界上就有一些奇怪的事情。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: There's some weirdness in the world.
segments.translation: 世界上总有一些奇怪的事。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Like knowing not to do something and then something happens.
segments.translation: 就像知道不做某事然后某事发生了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: There's some weirdness and knowing something's going to happen and you ignore that feeling and then something terrible happens.
segments.translation: 有一些奇怪的感觉，知道有些事情会发生，但你忽略了这种感觉，然后可怕的事情发生了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: You're like, fuck, I knew I shouldn't have gone there.
segments.translation: 你就像，操，我知道我不应该去那里。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: There's there's weirdness in the world.
segments.translation: 世界上总有一些奇怪的事。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And it's not necessarily just pattern recognition and understanding scenarios because you've experienced them before.
segments.translation: 这不一定只是模式识别和理解场景，因为你以前经历过它们。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: There's something to that too.
segments.translation: 这也是有原因的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: That's part of it too.
segments.translation: 这也是其中的一部分。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: But there's also something else.
segments.translation: 但还有其他事情。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: There's some weird connection that people have.
segments.translation: 人们之间有一些奇怪的联系。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: There's a thing that you, when you know someone's mad at you and they don't say anything like, what is this fucking weird energy?
segments.translation: 当你知道有人生你的气而他们却没有说什么时，你会想，这他妈的奇怪的能量是什么？

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I'm getting off this guy.
segments.translation: 我要摆脱这个家伙了

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: There's some stuff we're we're experiencing in the world that you can't put on a scale.
segments.translation: 我们在这个世界上正在经历的一些事情是无法用规模来衡量的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: You can't put a tape measure to it.
segments.translation: 你不能用卷尺测量它。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: You know, you can't, you can't measure its density, but it's there.
segments.translation: 你知道，你不能，你无法测量它的密度，但它就在那里。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: There's something.
segments.translation: 有东西。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And we have a very limited amount of senses in terms of our ability to see, feel, touch, smell.
segments.translation: 我们的感官非常有限，包括视觉、感觉、触觉、嗅觉。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: It's not enough.
segments.translation: 这还不够。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: It's probably some other stuff out there.
segments.translation: 那里可能还有其他东西。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: We don't the tools to measure, but it impacts us.
segments.translation: 我们没有衡量的工具，但它会影响我们。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: But we do have the tools to measure.
segments.translation: 但我们确实有衡量的工具。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So that's what attracted me to the rest of my career because exactly for the same reason you just said that people have experiences, oftentimes they feel pretty strange.
segments.translation: 这就是我余下职业生涯的吸引点，因为正如你刚才所说的，人们有经历，通常他们会感觉很奇怪。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And so they start looking for, well, what, what is that?
segments.translation: 所以他们开始寻找，嗯，那是什么？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So if you go to a like a conventional science spokesperson, they will echo back exactly what you're saying.
segments.translation: 因此，如果你去找传统科学发言人，他们会准确地回应你所说的话。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It's coincidence, It's a, it's frailty of memory, all of that stuff.
segments.translation: 这是巧合，这是记忆力的脆弱，所有这些东西。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: But I learned early on, even in college, that there is a branch of science that has studied these things.
segments.translation: 但我很早就知道，甚至在大学里，就有一个科学分支正在研究这些东西。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I mean, it's been going on since the late 1800s that the scientists have been interested in these kinds of phenomena.
segments.translation: 我的意思是，自 1800 年代末以来，科学家们就一直对此类现象感兴趣。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And science is really, really good at taking even strange subjective experiences and figuring out is that a coincidence or is that what, what is that?
segments.translation: 科学真的非常擅长接受甚至奇怪的主观经历，并弄清楚这是巧合还是那是什么？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Is it real?
segments.translation: 这是真的吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: That attracted me so.
segments.translation: 这太吸引我了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And it, it partially came out of reading a lot of science fiction.
segments.translation: 它部分来自于阅读大量科幻小说。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So your science fiction is saturated with these kinds of stories where the the element of the story is revolving around some kind of psychic or noetic thing.
segments.translation: 因此，你的科幻小说中充满了这类故事，其中故事的元素围绕着某种通灵或心灵的事物。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: The Force.
segments.translation: 原力。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Yeah, the the force in, in Dune, the series, Frank Herbert's Dune series, the whole thing about spice, Why did they have to take spice?
segments.translation: 是的，在《沙丘》系列中，弗兰克·赫伯特的《沙丘》系列中的力量，整个关于香料的事情，为什么他们必须采取香料？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Because that's the only way you can navigate when you're you're jumping through wormholes like you needed to know what you're about to expect in the other side.
segments.translation: 因为当你在虫洞中跳跃时，这是你导航的唯一方法，就像你需要知道在另一边会发生什么一样。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It just saturates novels and science fiction.
segments.translation: 它只是充斥着小说和科幻小说。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It's there.
segments.translation: 它就在那里。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And generally, if, if you have a topic that people are paying attention to like that and are very popular, it's because something is resonating.
segments.translation: 一般来说，如果你有一个人们如此关注并且非常受欢迎的话题，那是因为某些东西引起了共鸣。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Like if, if, if it was so strange that nobody even had a way of thinking about it, it wouldn't be popular.
segments.translation: 就像如果，如果，如果它是如此奇怪以至于没有人思考它，它就不会受欢迎。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: But it is, and it's perennially popular.
segments.translation: 但事实确实如此，而且它一直很受欢迎。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So.
segments.translation: 所以。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So I took the science fiction interest and as an even younger kid about fairy tales, which is saturated with these things too.
segments.translation: 所以我对科幻小说产生了兴趣，当我还是个小孩子的时候，我就对童话故事产生了兴趣，童话故事里也充满了这些东西。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And I thought, well, that I wonder if that's real.
segments.translation: 我想，好吧，我想知道这是否是真的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: But then you kind of get shuttled into a scientific career.
segments.translation: 但随后你就进入了科学事业。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And one thing that happens for fledgling engineers and scientists and for a lot of other academics is that you're being taught a set of assumptions about the way that the world works called materialism or physicalism.
segments.translation: 对于初出茅庐的工程师和科学家以及许多其他学者来说，发生的一件事是，你正在被教导一套关于世界运行方式的假设，称为唯物主义或物理主义。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And The thing is, you're not taught that that is a set of assumptions.
segments.translation: 问题是，你没有被告知这是一组假设。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: You take it for granted after a while, because after you go through college for 20 plus years and no one ever mentions that we're working under a set of assumptions and materialism.
segments.translation: 一段时间后你会认为这是理所当然的，因为当你读完大学二十多年后，没有人提到我们是在一系列假设和唯物主义下工作。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And no one ever talks about the philosophy of science, which is all about studying the assumptions.
segments.translation: 没有人谈论科学哲学，科学哲学就是研究假设。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And are they correct?
segments.translation: 它们正确吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Once you do start studying the philosophy of science, you find out that there's lots of different ways of understanding reality.
segments.translation: 一旦你开始研究科学哲学，你就会发现理解现实有很多不同的方式。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And so there's the whole materialistic side, which is really, really good at explaining aspects of the physical world.
segments.translation: 因此，存在整个唯物主义的一面，它非常非常擅长解释物理世界的各个方面。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It it gives us these kinds of technologies, but it doesn't explain subjective experience at all.
segments.translation: 它为我们提供了这些技术，但它根本无法解释主观体验。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And so that's, that's like a existing number one mystery in science today, because you have to challenge the idea that materialism is all there is.
segments.translation: 这就像当今科学界的一个头号谜团，因为你必须挑战唯物主义就是一切的观念。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And so people have weird experiences.
segments.translation: 所以人们会有奇怪的经历。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: They're talking about a more comprehensive way of understanding reality.
segments.translation: 他们正在谈论一种更全面的方式来理解现实。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: That's what's going on.
segments.translation: 这就是正在发生的事情。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And so that's that's why I end up writing a book like this.
segments.translation: 这就是我最终写这样一本书的原因。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So the magic here is not stage magic.
segments.translation: 所以这里的魔术不是舞台魔术。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It's it's the real magic, which we don't have a name for yet.
segments.translation: 这是真正的魔法，我们还没有给它命名。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: When they first started studying this in the 1800s, what were they specifically trying to isolate or figure out?
segments.translation: 当他们在 1800 年代第一次开始研究这个问题时，他们具体想分离或弄清楚什么？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Well, just like today, people would see apparitions, they would have the sense that there were telepathic connections between people, they'd have precognitions, and there was the beginning of figuring out ways of using experimental science to be able to study these things under controlled conditions.
segments.translation: 嗯，就像今天一样，人们会看到幻影，他们会感觉到人与人之间存在心灵感应联系，他们会有预知力，并且开始找出使用实验科学的方法，以便能够在受控条件下研究这些事物。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And, and the word control is important because it means you exclude coincidence by the design, and you exclude leakage of information.
segments.translation: 而且，文字控制很重要，因为它意味着您可以通过设计排除巧合，并排除信息泄漏。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: You exclude all kinds of things.
segments.translation: 你排除了各种各样的事情。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So the only thing leftover is if that telepathic thing was real, then we'd be able to see it in the lab.
segments.translation: 所以唯一剩下的就是如果心灵感应的东西是真实的，那么我们就可以在实验室中看到它。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And the short story is, yeah, so we're now 150 years past that, and we have very, very strong evidence that telepathy does exist.
segments.translation: 简而言之，是的，我们现在已经过去 150 年了，而且我们有非常非常有力的证据表明心灵感应确实存在。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: So what was the first evidence that they they were able to get out of these initial experiments?
segments.translation: 那么他们能够从这些最初的实验中获得的第一个证据是什么？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: They used to call it thought transference.
segments.translation: 他们过去称之为思想转移。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And so the methods they were using then would not pass muster.
segments.translation: 所以他们当时使用的方法是不合格的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Today they, they would have like 2 kids who say we can, we can, we can do telepathic transfer between US.
segments.translation: 今天，他们会有两个孩子说我们可以，我们可以，我们可以在美国之间进行心灵感应转移。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And then many times they would find that the kids were using some kind of signal.
segments.translation: 很多时候他们会发现孩子们正在使用某种信号。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And so that that wouldn't work today.
segments.translation: 所以今天这行不通。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Today people have to be strictly isolated.
segments.translation: 今天人们必须严格隔离。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Neither can know what the target is that they're trying to transfer to the other person.
segments.translation: 双方都不知道他们试图转移给对方的目标是什么。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And we do lots and lots of replications with lots of people.
segments.translation: 我们与很多人一起进行了很多很多的复制。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And so that that then forms a body of evidence where it becomes extremely difficult to think of what the flaw might be.
segments.translation: 这样就形成了一系列证据，很难想象可能存在的缺陷。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And in fact, we have skeptics about it who know the literature.
segments.translation: 事实上，了解文献的人对此持怀疑态度。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Their usual response now is either there's no plausible flaw that they can identify because a lot of time has been spent to figure out what might be a flaw.
segments.translation: 他们现在通常的反应是，要么没有他们可以识别的看似合理的缺陷，因为已经花费了大量时间来找出可能存在的缺陷。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And the second response, which is more recent now is we're not even going to look at the evidence because we know it's impossible, which is no longer a scientific argument, But that's that's the approach.
segments.translation: 第二个回应是最近出现的，我们甚至不去查看证据，因为我们知道这是不可能的，这不再是一个科学论证，但这就是方法。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: We're not going to look at the data.
segments.translation: 我们不会看数据。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: That's silly.
segments.translation: 那太愚蠢了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Yeah, well, it's really silly when you consider the intelligence agencies have spent an enormous amount of money in a considerable amount of time studying remote viewing.
segments.translation: 是的，嗯，当你考虑到情报机构在相当长的时间里花费了大量的资金来研究远程监控时，这真的很愚蠢。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Like, why?
segments.translation: 比如，为什么？

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Why would they invest that much time in nonsense?
segments.translation: 他们为什么要花那么多时间在废话上？

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Why would they invest that much time in something where there's no evidence whatsoever and they've never achieved positive results?
segments.translation: 他们为什么要在没有任何证据且从未取得积极成果的事情上投入那么多时间？

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: That doesn't seem to be correct.
segments.translation: 这似乎不正确。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: No, if you just, if you listen to the stories of the guys, like how put off and all these different people that have been involved in these remote viewing experiments, they had actionable data that they they, they derived specifically from remote viewing.

segments.text: I don't understand it.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: We, we had an experiment on a television show that I did where we had this guy who claimed to be a remote viewer, remote view this area and it was, he was off, but it was also under duress with cameras.
segments.translation: 我们，我们在一个电视节目上做了一个实验，我们让一个自称是远程观众的人远程观看这个区域，结果他不在，但也受到摄像机的胁迫。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Like is that the state of mind that you want to be in when you're trying to remove, you know, that's not ideal at all.
segments.translation: 就像当你试图消除时你想要处于的心态一样，你知道，这根本不理想。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And that is a factor, a major factor in whether or not you can understand intuition is where, what is your state of mind?
segments.translation: 这就是一个因素，你能不能理解直觉的一个主要因素在哪里，你的心态是什么？

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Are you in a place of complete anxiety and fear or are you totally relaxed and focused on what you're doing?
segments.translation: 您是否处于完全焦虑和恐惧的状态，或者您是否完全放松并专注于您正在做的事情？

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Is there any distractions?
segments.translation: 有什么干扰吗？

segments.text: What?
segments.translation: 什么？

segments.text: Is there something that could interrupt this state of mind that you're trying to achieve?
segments.translation: 有什么事情可以打断你想要达到的这种心态吗？

segments.text: Because there's different states of mind.
segments.translation: 因为心态不同。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: We know this, we can measure this.
segments.translation: 我们知道这一点，我们可以衡量这一点。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: We can measure the brain waves.
segments.translation: 我们可以测量脑电波。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: We can, we can, we understand that the state of mind, it's not a static thing like a toaster, you know, it's not on or off.
segments.translation: 我们可以，我们可以，我们理解心态，它不是像烤面包机那样静态的东西，你知道，它不是打开或关闭的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: There's a bunch of different shit going on in your brain, in your mind at any given time.
segments.translation: 在任何特定的时间，你的大脑里、你的脑海里都在发生着一堆不同的事情。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And so the idea that remote viewing, which is some very bizarre connection that some people have to reality that's nowhere near local.
segments.translation: 因此，远程观看的想法是一些人与现实相距甚远的一种非常奇怪的联系。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: They can describe things in detail.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Talk about submarines that are being constructed in the in Soviet Union, Like it's there's weird shit to that.
segments.translation: 谈论苏联正在建造的潜艇，就像有什么奇怪的事情一样。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And if you if you just dismiss that, you're being a fool.
segments.translation: 如果你不理睬这一点，那你就是个傻瓜。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: There's something there.
segments.translation: 那里有东西。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And the only way anybody figures out or something there is if you study it, if actually intelligent people are willing to look a little foolish and spend some time studying it.
segments.translation: 任何人弄清楚或存在某事的唯一方法就是如果你研究它，如果真正聪明的人愿意看起来有点愚蠢并花一些时间研究它。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Right, so that brings us to my next job.
segments.translation: 好的，这就是我的下一份工作。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So after I got my my doctorate, I started working at Bell Laboratories.
segments.translation: 因此，在获得博士学位后，我开始在贝尔实验室工作。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So it was the biggest laboratory in the world at the time is still the Bell System.
segments.translation: 所以当时世界上最大的实验室仍然是贝尔系统。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And because I was interested in these kinds of things for some of my time at Bell Labs, I started doing little psychic experiments involving mind matter interaction and also involving precognition.
segments.translation: 因为我在贝尔实验室的一段时间里对这些事情很感兴趣，所以我开始做一些涉及心灵物质相互作用和预知的小心灵实验。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So there's there's an ongoing link here that goes back to the Institute in Diabetic Sciences.
segments.translation: 因此，这里有一个持续的链接可以追溯到糖尿病科学研究所。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: In a strange way, Edgar Mitchell was gave the first money to Sri International, which is where he'll put off.
segments.translation: 以一种奇怪的方式，埃德加·米切尔（Edgar Mitchell）将第一笔钱交给了斯里国际公司（Sri International），而这正是他推迟的地方。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And Russ Targ was to do remote viewing studies.
segments.translation: 拉斯·塔格（Russ Targ）将进行远程观察研究。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: He also brought Yuri Geller to the United States and he brought Sri in a bunch of other places, including Bell Labs.
segments.translation: 他还将尤里·盖勒（Yuri Geller）带到了美国，并将斯里带到了许多其他地方，包括贝尔实验室。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So when I was working at the labs, I knew that there had been people who had seen some of the stuff that Geller did and I was doing these little psychic things.
segments.translation: 所以当我在实验室工作时，我知道有人见过盖勒所做的一些事情，而我正在做这些小小的灵媒事情。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So I asked for permission to be able to present some of the work I was doing at an annual conference of the Parapsychological Association, which is an affiliate of the largest scientific organization in the United States, the American Association for the Advancement of Science.
segments.translation: 因此，我请求允许在超心理学协会的年度会议上展示我所做的一些工作，该协会是美国最大的科学组织美国科学促进会的附属机构。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So many people don't know that the Parapsychological Association is one of the 200 some affiliates of the AAA S It's a legitimate scientific organization.
segments.translation: 很多人不知道超心理学协会是 AAA S 的 200 多个附属机构之一，它是一个合法的科学组织。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So I did this precognition test.
segments.translation: 所以我做了这个预知测试。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I asked for permission and I got permission.
segments.translation: 我请求许可并且得到了许可。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I don't need to give my presentation at the conference, but to use the Bell Labs imprimatur.
segments.translation: 我不需要在会议上发表演讲，但需要得到贝尔实验室的认可。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So I was giving this as some guy from Bell Labs talking to this audience.
segments.translation: 所以我是以贝尔实验室的某个人的身份向观众发表讲话的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Unbeknownst to me, there were a few people in the audience who came up afterwards and one of them said if there was an opening, would you you be interested in joining the Stargate program?
segments.translation: 不知不觉间，后来台下有几个人上来，其中一人说，如果有空缺，你有兴趣加入星门计划吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And so that was an offer I couldn't refuse.
segments.translation: 所以这是一个我无法拒绝的提议。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: That's one of these cases of that you have this door or you have that door.
segments.translation: 这就是你有这扇门或那扇门的情况之一。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Well, that door looked really interesting because it was known at the time that there were people at Sri doing this sort of thing.
segments.translation: 嗯，那扇门看起来真的很有趣，因为当时就知道 Sri 有人在做这种事情。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: But the classified portions were a rumor, like nobody knew what was really going on, right?
segments.translation: 但机密部分只是谣言，好像没有人知道到底发生了什么，对吧？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So I took a leave of absence.
segments.translation: 于是我请了假。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: That must have been exciting.
segments.translation: 那一定很令人兴奋。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Yeah.
segments.translation: 是的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: You get that offer?
segments.translation: 你收到那个报价了吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Yeah.
segments.translation: 是的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Stargate.
segments.translation: 星门。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Yeah, are you kidding?
segments.translation: 是啊，你在开玩笑吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Holy shit.
segments.translation: 天啊。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So I took a leave of absence for one year from Bell Labs, and so I went to Sri International.
segments.translation: 所以我从贝尔实验室请了一年假，然后去了斯里国际。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Hal Puthoff was my boss.
segments.translation: 哈尔·普索夫是我的老板。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And then Ed May, when Hal left in 1985, Ed May took over.
segments.translation: 然后是埃德·梅（Ed May），1985 年哈尔离开后，埃德·梅接任。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: He may not be a name that is known as well, but he was the director for 10 years.
segments.translation: 他的名字可能不太为人所知，但他担任导演已有10年了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And so I worked on that project and it took a long time to get the clearances because first of all, I didn't know anything about classification or anything.
segments.translation: 所以我参与了这个项目，花了很长时间才获得许可，因为首先，我对分类或任何东西一无所知。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: But I figured, well, maybe it's just secret.
segments.translation: 但我想，好吧，也许这只是秘密。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: No, it's just top secret.
segments.translation: 不，这只是最高机密。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: No, it's top secret SEI.
segments.translation: 不，这是绝密的 SEI。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: No, it's top secret SEI special access program, which means there's literally a book that you have to sign and you can see all the other people who have signed that book.
segments.translation: 不，这是绝密的 SEI 特殊访问计划，这意味着您实际上必须签署一本书，并且您可以看到签署该书的所有其他人。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Special access means even if you have a top secret clearance, you cannot know about this place.
segments.translation: 特殊通道意味着即使你有绝密权限，你也无法知道这个地方。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: You cannot know about the code word.
segments.translation: 你无法知道代码字。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: You can't.
segments.translation: 你不能。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The code word was classified so I mean, which seems kind of odd because if you have a code word it's not saying anything, but nevertheless that's how it worked.
segments.translation: 暗号是被分类的，所以我的意思是，这看起来有点奇怪，因为如果你有一个暗号，它不会说什么，但尽管如此，它就是这样工作的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Wow.
segments.translation: 哇。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So we were the research side of people who talk about Stargate.
segments.translation: 所以我们是谈论星际之门的人的研究方。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Mostly they're talking about the military side, the operational side.
segments.translation: 他们主要谈论的是军事方面、作战方面。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Well, we knew what they were doing, but our mission was different.
segments.translation: 好吧，我们知道他们在做什么，但我们的使命不同。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Our mission was figure out those questions that you're asking.
segments.translation: 我们的任务是弄清楚您提出的那些问题。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: How does this stuff work?
segments.translation: 这个东西是如何工作的？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Like, is it real?
segments.translation: 比如，这是真的吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Yes, some people are very talented.
segments.translation: 是的，有些人很有才华。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: What are the limits of it?
segments.translation: 它的局限性是什么？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Can you block it?
segments.translation: 你能阻止它吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Can you shield it?
segments.translation: 可以屏蔽一下吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Can you do camouflage?
segments.translation: 可以做迷彩吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And one of the main areas was, what's the difference between someone like Joe Mcmonagle, who's a superstar in this area?
segments.translation: 主要领域之一是，像乔·麦克莫纳格尔这样的人，这个领域的超级明星，有什么区别？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Why is he any different than anybody else?
segments.translation: 为什么他和其他人有什么不同？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Because like when I first met the Ingo Swann and Joe and a bunch of other people, they were the kind, they were so different than my stereotype of Madame Zodiac that they like, I'd say, you got to be kidding.
segments.translation: 因为就像我第一次见到 Ingo Swann 和 Joe 以及其他一些人时一样，他们就是这样的人，他们与我对十二宫夫人的刻板印象如此不同，以至于他们喜欢，我想说，你一定是在开玩笑。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: These people are remote viewers.
segments.translation: 这些人是远程观众。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: They're just like guys and gals.
segments.translation: 他们就像男孩和女孩一样。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And so every method was used to try to figure out is it psychological difference?
segments.translation: 于是用尽各种方法试图弄清楚这是否是心理差异？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Is it physiological?
segments.translation: 是生理性的吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Is it medical?
segments.translation: 是医疗的吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: What is it?
segments.translation: 它是什么？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And the answer was we couldn't find anything.
segments.translation: 答案是我们什么也没找到。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Now, there may be some background about the people themselves, but in terms of finding out something that we could use to select because the the Army and others were interested in getting lots of other people who would be talented too.
segments.translation: 现在，人们本身可能有一些背景，但就找出我们可以用来选择的东西而言，因为陆军和其他人有兴趣获得许多其他也有才华的人。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: So there's no consistent factors.
segments.translation: 所以没有一致的因素。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: No, there wasn't.
segments.translation: 不，没有。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Wasn't anything.
segments.translation: 本来就没什么啊

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Wow.
segments.translation: 哇。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So.
segments.translation: 所以。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: That seems crazy.
segments.translation: 这看起来很疯狂。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Except maybe talent.
segments.translation: 也许除了天赋。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Two things.
segments.translation: 有两件事。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Talent and openness.
segments.translation: 人才和开放。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So talent is natural talent.
segments.translation: 所以天赋是天生的天赋。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It's it did partially based on genetics.
segments.translation: 这部分是基于遗传学。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And openness is a psychological trait where you're simply open to experience.
segments.translation: 开放性是一种心理特征，你对体验持开放态度。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So people who tend to be to, to have like a certain way of thinking about things that are not not open to other stuff, they block it.
segments.translation: 因此，那些倾向于以某种方式思考事物而不对其他事物不开放的人，他们会阻止它。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: They could block it real good.
segments.translation: 他们可以很好地阻止它。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: People who are open to experience and willing to try new things, they in general tend to do better.
segments.translation: 那些对经验持开放态度并愿意尝试新事物的人，一般来说往往会做得更好。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So that brings us to talent, which I'll get to a little bit later, especially about the genetics of talent.
segments.translation: 这让我们谈到了人才，我稍后会谈到这个问题，特别是关于人才的遗传学。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So we didn't have the genetic tools at the time.
segments.translation: 所以我们当时没有遗传工具。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Now we do have the genetic tools.
segments.translation: 现在我们确实有了遗传工具。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And so we've done a couple of studies looking for what we call the PSI gene.
segments.translation: 因此，我们做了几项研究来寻找我们所说的 PSI 基因。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So we we think we're on to something.
segments.translation: 所以我们认为我们正在做某事。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: OK, so, so I work on Stargate for a year, the go back to Bell Labs and almost immediately get another invitation.
segments.translation: 好吧，我在《星际之门》工作了一年，然后回到贝尔实验室，几乎立刻就收到了另一份邀请。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It's one of these doors open again.
segments.translation: 其中一扇门再次打开。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: How would you like to go to Princeton?
segments.translation: 你想去普林斯顿怎么样？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Because at Princeton at the time was the Princeton Engineering Anomalies Research Laboratory.
segments.translation: 因为当时在普林斯顿有普林斯顿工程异常研究实验室。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It was the lab doing PSI research that was headed by the Dean of the School of Engineering.
segments.translation: 这是一个由工程学院院长领导的从事PSI研究的实验室。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And so that lab went almost for 30 years doing mindmatter interaction, doing a remote viewing and a bunch of other stuff at Princeton.
segments.translation: 因此，普林斯顿实验室花了近 30 年的时间进行心灵互动、远程观察和其他一系列工作。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So my position was in the psych department because that's where I had my PhD, but to lead a program among many departments, one of which was the pair lab.
segments.translation: 所以我的职位是在心理学系，因为那是我获得博士学位的地方，但要领导多个系之间的一个项目，其中之一是结对实验室。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And the idea was in order to have any chance of beginning to understand this stuff, you need to pull in every discipline because it's way too big.
segments.translation: 这个想法是为了有机会开始理解这些东西，你需要吸收每一个学科，因为它太大了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It's it's too complicated for a single discipline.
segments.translation: 对于单一学科来说它太复杂了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So we had the philosophy department and the psychology department and civil engineering and the pair lab and a bunch of other departments.
segments.translation: 所以我们有哲学系、心理学系、土木工程系、结对实验室和许多其他系系。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: My job is to sort of corral it together to create multidisciplinary research projects.
segments.translation: 我的工作是将其整合在一起创建多学科研究项目。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And I was told in day one, that's impossible.
segments.translation: 第一天我就被告知，这是不可能的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: This is a job you cannot do well.
segments.translation: 这是一项你无法做好的工作。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Why?
segments.translation: 为什么？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I mean, we had the money for it.
segments.translation: 我的意思是，我们有钱。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And the answer is that in the academic world, you succeed within silos, You know, an enormous amount about a very particular kind of topic.
segments.translation: 答案是，在学术界，你在孤岛中取得成功，你知道，关于一个非常特殊的话题的大量内容。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Like even in the psych department there you have cognitive psychologists, perceptual psychologists, social psychologists, and on and on and on.
segments.translation: 就像在心理学系一样，你也有认知心理学家、知觉心理学家、社会心理学家等等。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: They don't even talk to each other because it's outside of your discipline, outside the little silo.
segments.translation: 他们甚至不互相交谈，因为这超出了你的纪律，超出了小筒仓。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: My job was to sort of mash it together and it was ridiculously complicated.
segments.translation: 我的工作就是将它们混合在一起，这非常复杂。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Was there resistance?
segments.translation: 有抵抗吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Oh my God, Resistance is not quite strong enough.
segments.translation: 天哪，抵抗力还不够强。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It's like each one of the departments was getting money from this big grant that we had, so they were willing to play the game, but when it actually came down to doing some kind of a cross filtering, no.
segments.translation: 就好像每个部门都从我们的这笔大笔拨款中获得了资金，所以他们愿意玩这个游戏，但当它实际上归结为进行某种交叉过滤时，却没有。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Why didn't they want to collaborate?
segments.translation: 他们为什么不愿意合作？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Because everything of value in the academic world is in your silo.
segments.translation: 因为学术界所有有价值的东西都在你的筒仓里。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And so if you're trying to work across silos again, even within the same department, social psychology and perceptual psychology might not even talk to each other.
segments.translation: 因此，如果您尝试再次跨部门工作，即使在同一部门内，社会心理学和感知心理学甚至可能无法相互交流。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And they had their offices are right next to each other, but that's simply the way that's.
segments.translation: 他们的办公室彼此相邻，但事实就是如此。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Sane.
segments.translation: 理智。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Yeah, but it also, it sort of makes sense when you think about it, to become an expert in something takes 20 years from from the university and then the rest of your academic career just to keep up with it.
segments.translation: 是的，但仔细想想，这也是有道理的，从大学毕业后要花 20 年时间才能成为某个领域的专家，然后用剩下的学术生涯才能跟上它的步伐。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So it kind of makes sense that you don't want to start turning your attention off to something else because you're not in that department anymore.
segments.translation: 因此，你不想因为你不再在那个部门而开始将注意力转移到其他事情上，这是有道理的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So it's a problem and it's always been there.
segments.translation: 所以这是一个问题，而且一直存在。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It's not getting any better either.
segments.translation: 情况也没有好转。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Well, it seems like there should be a way to fix that.
segments.translation: 嗯，看来应该有办法解决这个问题。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: The ultimate goal should be whatever we're all working on collectively should benefit mankind.
segments.translation: 最终目标应该是我们共同努力的一切都应该造福于人类。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And if you're in the psychology industry, which you are if you're teaching psychology, if you're working on psychology, you should want to get involved in this.
segments.translation: 如果你在心理学行业，如果你在教授心理学，如果你在研究心理学，你应该想参与其中。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: The fact they're all siloed off like that seems insane.
segments.translation: 事实上，他们都像这样被孤立起来，这似乎很疯狂。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Yeah.
segments.translation: 是的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So the the approach that's sometimes taken in the academic world is to create a center, Center for the study of fill in the blank that brings in people from different disciplines and then a kind of force together.
segments.translation: 因此，学术界有时采取的方法是创建一个中心，填补空白的研究中心，将来自不同学科的人们聚集在一起，然后形成一种力量。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: But these people from different disciplines probably are already working on important stuff to them and this is taking away from their time.
segments.translation: 但这些来自不同学科的人可能已经在从事对他们来说重要的事情，这占用了他们的时间。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It, it could be, except that depending on the nature of the work, it may be something that requires another discipline.
segments.translation: 它，它可能是，除了根据工作的性质，它可能需要另一种纪律。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So you might have somebody in computer science who's working on that and then you have somebody in psychology who's interested in the human side.
segments.translation: 所以你可能会有计算机科学领域的人在研究这个问题，然后你会有心理学领域的人对人性的一面感兴趣。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Like how do you connect the computer and the people?
segments.translation: 比如你如何连接计算机和人？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Well, there's a sub discipline called human factors.
segments.translation: 嗯，有一个子学科叫做人为因素。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: That's where I was working in Bell Labs because I had engineering and psychology.
segments.translation: 这就是我在贝尔实验室工作的地方，因为我拥有工程学和心理学专业。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So you kind of mashed those two together and then you could actually learn some new stuff.
segments.translation: 所以你可以将这两者混合在一起，然后你实际上可以学到一些新东西。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: That's a value to both and also you.
segments.translation: 这对双方和你来说都是有价值的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: That's how you create new disciplines.
segments.translation: 这就是创建新学科的方式。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: That's how the discipline of neuroscience began.
segments.translation: 这就是神经科学学科的开始。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So you go back now, it's more like 60 to 70 years ago, somebody noticed that you have all these people in biology and all these people looking at cells and people looking at things having to do with the nervous system that were all different disciplines.
segments.translation: 所以你现在回过头来看，更像是 60 到 70 年前，有人注意到生物学领域有很多人，所有这些人都在研究细胞，还有人在研究与神经系统有关的东西，这些人都是不同的学科。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So a large foundation came along and said, I think we need to create a discipline of the neurosciences, and they threw enough money at it to bring people together, and that formed a new discipline.
segments.translation: 因此，一个大型基金会出现并说，我认为我们需要创建一门神经科学学科，他们投入了足够的资金来将人们聚集在一起，这就形成了一个新的学科。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So I work in the area of consciousness studies, which is only now starting to become its own discipline because before that it was maybe a few philosophers interested in it and anesthesiologists, and that's it.
segments.translation: 所以我在意识研究领域工作，这个领域现在才开始成为自己的学科，因为在此之前可能只有一些哲学家和麻醉师对它感兴趣，仅此而已。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: But it's changing.
segments.translation: 但情况正在改变。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: So when you were at Princeton, what, what specifically did, how did you start it?
segments.translation: 那么当你在普林斯顿时，你具体做了什么，你是如何开始的？

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Like what?
segments.translation: 比如什么？

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: What specifically were you working on initially?
segments.translation: 您最初具体从事什么工作？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Well, besides trying to get people to talk to each other, which was frustrating.
segments.translation: 嗯，除了试图让人们互相交谈之外，这很令人沮丧。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Big.
segments.translation: 大的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Task.
segments.translation: 任务。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So one of the things I did was meta analysis.
segments.translation: 所以我做的一件事就是荟萃分析。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So this is a way of taking the results of individual experiments that are similar to each other, like telepathy experiments, and putting them all together with a statistical method to see whether independent people are able to replicate the same thing.
segments.translation: 因此，这是一种将彼此相似的单个实验的结果（例如心灵感应实验）放在一起，并用统计方法将它们放在一起，看看独立的人是否能够复制相同的事情。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It's called meta analysis, meta meaning it's like an analysis of analysis.
segments.translation: 这叫做元分析，元的意思是它就像分析的分析。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And so it answers 2 questions.
segments.translation: 所以它回答了两个问题。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: One is if this is really real in the scientific sense, then other independent people ought to be able to do the same experiment and get the same result.
segments.translation: 一是如果这在科学意义上确实是真实的，那么其他独立的人应该能够做同样的实验并得到同样的结果。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So that's one part.
segments.translation: 这就是一部分。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The other part is if you do have a lot of people doing the same experiment, then what is the overall result?
segments.translation: 另一部分是，如果确实有很多人做同样的实验，那么总体结果是什么？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It's like 1 gigantic experiment now.
segments.translation: 现在这就像一个巨大的实验。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So I, I did a number of meta analysis, ended up writing a book on it that nobody wanted to buy.
segments.translation: 所以我做了很多元分析，最终写了一本没有人愿意买的书。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So I just sat there and then I was doing experiments on precognition as part of my job.
segments.translation: 所以我就坐在那里，然后做预知实验，作为我工作的一部分。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And because of my engineering background, I was using the the latest version of machine learning at the time, which was neural networks and applying it to the data from the pair lab to see if you know when you do an experiment involving mindmatter interaction, usually use a random number generator.
segments.translation: 由于我的工程背景，我当时使用的是最新版本的机器学习，即神经网络，并将其应用到结对实验室的数据中，看看你是否知道当你做涉及心灵交互的实验时，通常会使用随机数生成器。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And you ask them, buddy, this thing is you tell them this is going to push out a whole bunch of bits, random bits.
segments.translation: 你问他们，伙计，这就是你告诉他们这将推出一大堆比特，随机比特。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And I want you to make more one bits than 0 bits.
segments.translation: 我希望你制作的 1 位多于 0 位。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: That's your task.
segments.translation: 这就是你的任务。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So they press a button and they get some kind of result and now make more 0 bits and now don't do anything.
segments.translation: 所以他们按下一个按钮，他们得到某种结果，现在产生更多的 0 位，现在什么也不做。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So this is a three different kinds of tasks in one session.
segments.translation: 所以这是在一个会话中完成三种不同类型的任务。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And So what, what they were finding was that in general, if you run a lot of people and this kind of task, yes, their intention makes the bits go in the direction that you want.
segments.translation: 那么，他们发现，一般来说，如果你管理很多人和这种任务，是的，他们的意图会让这些部分朝着你想要的方向发展。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So you aim high, it goes up aimed at low, it goes down South on.
segments.translation: 所以你的目标高，目标低，它就往上走，它就往南走。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So the question then is not everybody can do that.
segments.translation: 所以问题是不是每个人都能做到这一点。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Some people get the opposite result.
segments.translation: 有些人得到相反的结果。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So some people get really good on making it go high, but they can't make it go low.
segments.translation: 所以有些人很擅长让它走高，但他们无法让它走低。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So the idea came about there's or something like a signature that was from each person.
segments.translation: 所以这个想法就产生了，每个人都有签名之类的东西。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: People had a way of interacting with the machine that made it do certain things that was unique to them.
segments.translation: 人们有一种与机器交互的方式，使其能够做一些对他们来说独一无二的事情。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: But overall it worked out.
segments.translation: 但总的来说，它成功了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So I started using neural networks to see if I could train a neural network to tell who was doing the task based on how the random bits were working.
segments.translation: 因此，我开始使用神经网络，看看是否可以训练一个神经网络，根据随机位的工作原理来判断谁在执行任务。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And it turns out you can.
segments.translation: 事实证明你可以。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So when I left Princeton, because it was getting way too frustrating, I took that just.
segments.translation: 所以当我离开普林斯顿时，因为这太令人沮丧了，我就接受了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Trying to get people to work together.
segments.translation: 试图让人们一起工作。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Trying to do this multidisciplinary teams.
segments.translation: 尝试做这个多学科团队。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Yeah.
segments.translation: 是的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And as I told you the first day I was there for the job, I was told, by the way, you have you have an impossible job.
segments.translation: 正如我第一天告诉你的那样，我被告知，顺便说一句，你有一份不可能的工作。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It's necessary though, because this was part of the grant.
segments.translation: 但这是必要的，因为这是赠款的一部分。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: What you're doing is part of the grant, so you have to do it anyway.
segments.translation: 你所做的事情是补助金的一部分，所以无论如何你都必须这样做。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And I did it for three years.
segments.translation: 我这样做了三年。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And then they decided I don't want to do that anymore.
segments.translation: 然后他们决定我不想再这样做了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: But so I went back to to industry.
segments.translation: 但我还是回到了工业界。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: But I specifically told the people I was interviewing with, I want to pursue this, like this is the beginning of a technology where that will have a machine identify who you are and your intention, kind of like Neuralink, except there's no connection.
segments.translation: 但我特别告诉我采访的人，我想追求这一点，就像这是一项技术的开始，让机器识别你是谁和你的意图，有点像 Neuralink，只不过没有连接。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: There's nothing going in the brain.
segments.translation: 脑子里什么也没有。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It's purely intention.
segments.translation: 这纯粹是意图。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So I did end up working for a company outside of Washington, DC, where part of my work was doing exactly that.
segments.translation: 所以我最终确实在华盛顿特区以外的一家公司工作，我的部分工作就是做这件事。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: We're using more advanced neural networks with random number generators and got to the point where we're about to set a patent for this device because it worked.
segments.translation: 我们正在使用带有随机数生成器的更先进的神经网络，并且我们即将为该设备设置专利，因为它有效。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And the head of the organization at the time was a retired general who had a buddy who was an Admiral.
segments.translation: 当时这个组织的负责人是一位退役将军，他有一个哥们是海军上将。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And he said the the Navy's interested in this kind of for obvious reasons, they want ways of communicating with submarines.
segments.translation: 他表示，海军对这种方式感兴趣的原因显而易见，他们想要与潜艇进行通信的方式。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So at that point, we're like right on the edge of doing that.
segments.translation: 所以在这一点上，我们正处于这样做的边缘。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And we get bought by another company.
segments.translation: 然后我们被另一家公司收购了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And the new company said, you're not going to work on that anymore.
segments.translation: 新公司说，你不会再从事这个工作了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So the wheels internally, it started, it was like golden handcuffs.
segments.translation: 所以内部的轮子启动了，就像金手铐一样。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: A lot of money.
segments.translation: 很多钱。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Let's, I mean, it's a very good position, but I didn't really want to do that anymore.
segments.translation: 我的意思是，这是一个非常好的职位，但我真的不想再这样做了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Did they have a RE?
segments.translation: 他们有 RE 吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Was it a profitable issue?
segments.translation: 这是一个有利可图的问题吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The vice president in charge of the lab did not believe that it was possible.
segments.translation: 负责实验室的副院长并不认为这是可能的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Oh God.
segments.translation: 天啊。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: They also didn't look at the data, of course.
segments.translation: 当然，他们也没有查看数据。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So he said no, we're not going to do that.
segments.translation: 所以他说不，我们不会那样做。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: He doesn't want to be silly.
segments.translation: 他不想犯傻。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Yeah.
segments.translation: 是的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So, I mean, it's so frustrating.
segments.translation: 所以，我的意思是，这太令人沮丧了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: You have it worked.
segments.translation: 你已经成功了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: We have a thing here.
segments.translation: 我们这里有一件事。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It's working.
segments.translation: 它正在发挥作用。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: No, he just, he didn't want to do it.
segments.translation: 不，他只是，他不想这么做。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
